The strategies

A rules-based monthly momentum strategy for Indian stocks: own the market's strongest emerging companies, let winners run, and stop new buying when the broad market weakens. It comes in two forms. MIP8-XL100-G3-CS is the one 3AK-Cworks trades live; it adds gold when gold leads and keeps idle cash earning. MIP8-XL100 is the same stock strategy on its own, for investors who do not want gold or a cash fund.

3AK-CWORKS Platform tour

See the whole market. Act on evidence.

3AK-Cworks is a fully autonomous, systematic wealth-management system. Every evening it ingests the full NSE market, rebuilds its own sector and industry indices, measures market breadth from every angle, and turns it all into decisions that the strategies, including the MIP8 momentum family, execute by rule.

2,579NSE stocks tracked daily
15 yrsof exchange history, incl. delisted stocks
199synthetic sector, group and industry indices
170+market-breadth measures every session
3intelligence engines: market, sector, stock
Dailyautomated data-to-decision run after every close
3AK-Cworks · Cockpit, the evening read
How it is organised

One top-down path, from the whole market to a single order

Step 1 · Market

Is it a good time to be invested?

Breadth, regime and market intelligence decide how much risk to take.

Step 2 · Sectors

Where is the money going?

Our own sector and industry indices show leadership, rotation and seasonality.

Step 3 · Stocks

Which names are leading?

Visual lookups, fundamentals, super charts, multi-stock grids and scans.

Step 4 · Strategy

Execute without emotion

Rules turn the evidence into orders, placed and monitored automatically.

Step 1 · Market

Market breadth and intelligence, measured not guessed

An index can rise while most stocks fall. 3AK-Cworks reads what is happening underneath the index, every session, across the entire market.

Reports · Breadth
Detailed reporting

Breadth dashboard

The index chart, with its market regime shaded in, sits above the breadth that drives it.

  • Share of stocks above key moving averages, advancers vs decliners, turnover and volume
  • Plain-English reading of what the market is doing and what a trader should do about it
  • Filters for F&O, price, market cap, sector and price band
Reports · Market Breadth Monitor
Breadth intelligence

Market Breadth Monitor

A day-by-day table of breadth measures with a market stance on top. Each reading comes with the evidence behind it.

  • Exposure dial from 1 (sit out) to 5 (go big), backed by 15 years of history
  • 4% movers, breakouts vs breakdowns, 52-week highs and lows, MA breadth, breadth thrusts
  • Each cell coloured by how unusual it is, so the eye goes straight to what changed
Reports · Breadth charts

Breadth charts

Every breadth measure as its own chart, with the index overlaid. Stack any measures into a custom view with a synced crosshair to see how they line up over time.

Reports · Market Intelligence

Market Intelligence

Nine engines score buying pressure, selling pressure, leadership, money flow, volatility and more. It also finds the most similar markets in 14 years of history and shows what happened next.

Step 2 · Sectors & industries

Our own sector and industry indices, built from the ground up

Exchange sector indices are few and dominated by large companies. 3AK-Cworks classifies every stock at three levels (sector, industry group and industry) and builds its own equal-weighted index for every group with enough members: 199 indices in all.

Sectors · Charts
Synthesised indices

Sector charts

Every sector on one screen, ranked by any measure. Click a sector to open its industry groups, then its industries, then the stocks inside.

  • Sector → industry group → industry → stock, in four clicks
  • Relative strength, moving averages and candles on every card
Sectors · Lookup (Visual)
Visual lookup

One sector, every measure, at a glance

Pick any sector, industry group or industry and see its own index above a grid of small charts: relative strength, breadth, momentum, money flow, delivery and volatility over recent sessions.

  • What stands out: a short, plain-English list of the readings that are unusual today
  • Each reading is coloured against the group's own history, not just its size
Sectors · Rotation

Rotation

A rotation map shows every sector's strength and momentum against the market. You can see leadership arriving before it is obvious on a price chart.

Sectors · Intelligence

Sector Intelligence

A tailwind board ranks every sector, industry group and industry by how strongly it is leading, names the leading stocks inside each, and flags groups that are turning up or fading. It can be tuned to swing, positional or investor horizons.

Sectors · Seasonality
Base rates

Seasonality

How the indices and every sector have behaved in the coming months in past years, which groups usually beat the market and which lagged, and what has followed a losing streak.

  • A base rate, not a forecast: each month shows how many past years went the same way
  • Shown beside today's momentum, which has been the stronger guide
Step 3 · Stocks

From one super chart to the whole industry at a glance

Every stock carries dozens of daily metrics and its company fundamentals. The stock workspace lets you study one name in depth, compare a whole industry side by side, or search the market for a pattern.

Charts · Super chart
Super charts

One chart, every lens

A full charting workspace built for Indian markets.

  • Daily, weekly and monthly views side by side
  • Delivery %, relative strength vs index, sector and industry, RSI bands, base boxes
  • Circuit band and F&O status at a glance; colour-labelled watchlists with keyboard navigation
Stocks · Charts
Many stocks together

Multi-stock charts

Pick an industry and see its sector index, its industry index and every member stock in one grid. Switch to a list for returns, relative strength, turnover and delivery.

  • Sort the grid by any of dozens of metrics
  • Filter out circuit-band, illiquid or tiny stocks with one saved setting
Stocks · Lookup (Visual)
Visual lookup

One stock in depth

The stock's chart and stage on top, with its industry group and industry charts a click away. Below, every metric as its own small chart: trend, relative strength, momentum, turnover, delivery and power days.

  • What stands out: the few readings that matter today, and whether the move is the stock's own or its industry's
  • One click to the company's fundamentals or the full super chart
Stocks · Fundamentals

Fundamentals

Valuation, returns on capital, debt, growth and shareholding at a glance; the last four quarters with year-on-year and quarter-on-quarter change; plain-English highlights; and charts of sales, margins, profit and EPS over the years.

Stocks · Scan Builder

Scan Builder

Build a scan from any combination of indicators, run it on today or any past date, save it as a template, and open the results straight into the multi-stock charts.

Step 4 · Strategy & execution

The part investors never see, and the part that matters most

The screens are for people. Underneath, the same data drives strategies that run themselves.

Clean data, every evening

Prices, indicators, delivery, fundamentals and classifications refresh automatically after every close, with health checks on every step.

Research with a high bar

Ideas must hold up on 15 years of exchange data, including delisted companies, and after costs and tax, before any capital touches them. Most ideas fail that bar, and that is the point.

Hands-off execution

Strategies place, track and reconcile their own orders through the broker, with health checks, alerts and an audit trail on every step. No emotional overrides.

The approach

Emerging leaders, gold when it leads, cash that earns

Buy strength

Each month the strategy ranks the NSE universe on the strength and steadiness of its price leadership.

New money goes to challengers

New buying favours emerging leaders over the market's largest companies. A holding is never sold for growing large: a winner keeps its place.

Gold competes too

Gold is ranked on the same terms as stocks and can take a limited share of the portfolio, only while it leads.

Cash keeps working

When conditions weaken, new stock buying stops and cash builds up. That cash sits in a liquid-fund ETF, and gold can still be bought if it is leading.

Gold and cash

Two quiet helpers for the weak phases

Momentum in Indian mid and small caps comes in bursts. Gold and a cash fund carry the portfolio between them.

Rare

Gold is a guest, not a fixture. It led strongly enough to be owned in 10 separate periods since 2012; most of the time the strongest stocks outrank it.

2025–26

Its largest contribution came in the 2025–26 precious-metals rally, while mid and small caps stalled. Treat that as one episode, not a yearly source of return.

~6% on cash

Idle cash is held in a liquid-fund ETF. Short-term gains on gold and on the cash fund are taxed at the investor's income slab; the figures here include that tax.

What to expect

A momentum strategy, with the same bumps

~1 in 2

Trades that make money (52%). The average winner gained +44% and the average loser lost −14%.

30%+

Expect a fall of 30% or more from a peak at some point; the 14-year test's deepest was −38.0%. When gold leads it can be a meaningful share of the portfolio.

91 days

Median holding period, with about 44 trades a year. Winners are not trimmed, so a single strong name can grow to a large share of the portfolio.

About these numbers. The performance figures come from backtesting on clean exchange data (the 14-year test includes companies that later delisted) and from the MIP8-XL100-G3-CS Model Portfolio, which applies the same rules to 2026 market data from a ₹10 lakh start. They are historical simulation results and cannot guarantee future returns.

The market is supreme. The strategy adapts to the market, holding back new stock buying and building cash when conditions weaken. In a prolonged weak market it cannot manufacture returns.

Costs and taxes. Returns are net of STT, brokerage, exchange and SEBI fees, GST, stamp duty and slippage (0.27% per side). It also includes about 6% a year earned on uninvested cash parked in a liquid-fund ETF (an assumed rate; the fund's actual yield varies). "Post-tax" applies Indian capital-gains tax to each financial year's realised gains: 20% short-term on equity (15% before July 2024), the slab rate on short-term gold ETF gains and on the liquid-fund yield, with losses set off within the year. Indices are price indices, taxed once at exit as long-term gains. Actual results will vary with entry date, execution prices, portfolio size and the investor's tax position.

Equity investments carry risk, including loss of capital. This document is for information only and is not an offer or investment advice. Data to 23 Oct 2026 (14-year test to 22 Oct 2026).

The approach

Same stock discipline, nothing else

Buy strength

Each month the strategy ranks the NSE universe on the strength and steadiness of its price leadership.

New money goes to challengers

New buying favours emerging leaders over the market's largest companies. A holding is never sold for growing large: a winner keeps its place.

Let winners compound

Positions are held for as long as they stay among the leaders, often for many months. Laggards are replaced, not averaged down.

Respect the market

A market-trend safeguard halts new buying when conditions weaken, so cash builds up naturally in bad phases. Here that cash is simply held.

Why choose it

Pure equity, for those who want it

The stock side of the live strategy, without the two additions.

No gold

The portfolio holds Indian stocks only. It gives up the help gold has given in some weak phases for mid and small caps, and the slab-rate tax on short-term gold gains.

No cash fund

Uninvested money is not swept into a liquid fund, so it earns nothing in these figures. Investors can still park it as they choose.

Model Portfolio · 2026

₹10 lakh from 1 January 2026, run on the rules

The MIP8-XL100 Model Portfolio applies the strategy month by month from cash on 1 January 2026, in a year in which the Nifty 50 is −13.5% and the Nifty MidSmallcap 400 −5.7% to 23 Oct 2026. It is a simulation on 2026 market data; figures are pre-tax and net of all trading costs.

What to expect

A momentum strategy, with the same bumps

~1 in 2

Trades that make money (52%). The average winner gained +44% and the average loser lost −14%.

30%+

Expect a fall of 30% or more from a peak at some point; the 14-year test's deepest was −38.4%.

91 days

Median holding period, with about 43 trades a year. Winners are not trimmed, so a single strong name can grow to a large share of the portfolio.

About these numbers. The performance figures come from backtesting on clean exchange data (the 14-year test includes companies that later delisted) and from the MIP8-XL100 Model Portfolio, which applies the same rules to 2026 market data from a ₹10 lakh start. They are historical simulation results and cannot guarantee future returns.

The market is supreme. The strategy adapts to the market, holding back new stock buying and building cash when conditions weaken. In a prolonged weak market it cannot manufacture returns.

Costs and taxes. Returns are net of STT, brokerage, exchange and SEBI fees, GST, stamp duty and slippage (0.27% per side). Uninvested cash earns nothing in these figures. "Post-tax" applies Indian capital-gains tax to each financial year's realised gains: 20% short-term on equity (15% before July 2024), with losses set off within the year. Indices are price indices, taxed once at exit as long-term gains. Actual results will vary with entry date, execution prices, portfolio size and the investor's tax position.

Equity investments carry risk, including loss of capital. This document is for information only and is not an offer or investment advice. Data to 23 Oct 2026 (14-year test to 22 Oct 2026).
